result:
Review of `main..review` complete — 3 findings reported (1 correctness, 1 docs, 1 test-coverage), ranked above.

The diff itself (redirecting analytics/cache writes to `/tmp` on Vercel via the new `dataDir()` helper) is structurally sound: both finder agents confirmed every call site already tolerates write failures, no edge-runtime or split-path issues exist, and no other persistence code was left un-migrated. Three of the six candidate findings were dropped in verification — most notably a claimed cross-container cache-poisoning loop, which I refuted by tracing that the cache write and its parse-failure removal happen within the same request on the same container.

The one finding worth acting on before merge: `process.env.VERCEL` is likely also set in local dev when env vars come from the Vercel CLI (`vercel dev`, or `vercel env pull` → `.env.local`), which would silently move local persistence to `/tmp` and defeat the cache-replay workflow. Gating on `VERCEL_ENV` or an explicit override would be more precise.

Sources: [Vercel system environment variables](https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables/system-environment-variables), [vercel env CLI docs](https://vercel.com/docs/cli/env)
